ORAL ORDER Heard Mr N.J. Shah, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the applicant-State and perused the record and proceedings of Criminal Case No.2684 of 2000 of the Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Valsad.

2 The applicant has preferred this application under section 378(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code,
1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code') seeking leave to appeal to challenge the judgment and order dated 7th August 2015 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Valsad in Criminal Case No.2684 of 2000 whereby the respondents are acquitted under section 235(1) of the Code for the offence punishable under section 7(2)(5) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
3 I have perused the record and proceedings and the  impugned judgment.

sentences.text: HC-NIC Page 1 of 2 Created On Sun Feb 28 05:
R/CR.MA/254/2016 ORDER there was breach of mandatory provisions of section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The learned trial Judge has discussed the evidence and the provisions of section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act in paragraph 12 of the impugned judgment.

Considering the nature of the breach of the provisions of section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act which are held to be mandatory in nature by various decisions of this Court, I am of the opinion that no case is made out to grant the application seeking leave to prefer appeal.
As a corollary to the dismissal of the application for leave to prefer the appeal, criminal appeal also stands dismissed.
Record and proceedings be remitted back to the trial court forthwith.
